main_body: A tiled blue-grey roof on two wooden posts, with a gray stone water-trough counter below it
top_band: Counter at x=16: light gray rim row 30, blue water rows 31-34, light front rim row 35 (rows 30-35). Roof: light ridge rows 1-2 over a tile slope in rows 3-14.
evidence: The counter reads as a 3/4 piece. Its light rim (row 30) and blue water surface (rows 31-34) form a top of about 6 rows, closed by a light front-edge line at row 35. Below that is a mid-gray front face (rows 36-42) that is clearly darker, with a step of about 50 L. The roof has a tapered trapezoid silhouette with a light ridge at rows 1-2 and a scalloped slope, so its top slope reads as a visible surface, though it is mostly a front-facing slope. The 2px ridge on its own would be weak, but together with the slope and the dark eave rows 15-17 the roof is acceptable. The posts are vertical supports and need no top. No receding side faces are drawn.

style.evidence: The measured facts put the candidate well below both references: 9 colours per tile against 17 and 20, and 23 distinct colours against 40 and 38. All of its dark edge pixels are neutral (100%), against 1% and 33% for the references, so the outline is the near-black sticker line rather than a tinted material tone. The roof has about 4-5 steps with vertical tile stripes but little per-tile texture. The gray counter front (rows 37-42) is a flat 6-row block of one colour, and the posts are simple flat bands. Flat-fill coverage is only 11%, similar to the cheese stall, but the piece is thinner, flatter and more sticker-like than either reference.
